question.text: Under Ch 12, the 'Indenture of Trust' is relevant to institutional investor DD PRIMARILY because:

answer.text: It sets the Manager's performance fee.
It determines the fund's hurdle rate and clawback terms.
It specifies the exit strategy and IPO preferences.
It determines the nature of trust (Determinate vs Indeterminate) and the applicable tax rates — impacting beneficial ownership and whether tax is paid by the fund or by investors.

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 331 of the workbook states that the Indenture of Trust / Trust Deed is an important document to determine the tax liability of institutional investors and the beneficial ownership in the Trust structure. Determinate vs Indeterminate trust status drives the applicable income-tax rates and whether income tax is paid by the fund or by the investors. The Trap: A, B, C all relate to terms typically found in the PPM or Contribution Agreement, not the Trust Deed. Note: Page 334 supports providing an external legal-counsel tax-structuring opinion on the trust's determinacy where available, as part of the institutional investor DD pack.
